messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"The air feels lighter in some corners—old friends are exchanging letters again, and the markets hum with quiet energy—but the walls still stand, just a little more worn. The gardeners are tired, and the fence posts, though steady, lean differently in the wind. Best to tend your own plot carefully, and trust the soil, not the season."*"
Sender 2: "*"The weather’s been unusually calm lately—no storms on the horizon, but the old trees are whispering about roots shifting underground. Best to keep our conversations light at gatherings, and trust that the usual routines will hold for now."*"
Sender 3: "*"The air feels different—less like winter’s stillness and more like the pause before a storm. The old rules still hold, but the hands enforcing them seem less steady, and the streets hum with quiet questions. Let’s keep our circles small, our steps careful, and our ears open—this could be the calm before something, but we won’t know which way the wind will blow until it’s already moving us."*"
Sender 4: "*"The weather looks calm for now—no storms on the horizon, but the wind is shifting. Best to keep your boots clean and your bags packed, just in case."*"
Sender 5: "*"The air feels different—less certain, but not yet broken. The regime’s grip is slipping, but they’re still dangerous, and the streets are full of anger without a clear path forward. Let’s stay sharp, keep our circles small, and watch for the next move—whether it’s theirs or ours."*"
Sender 6: "*"The weather looks stable for now—no storms on the horizon, but the wind’s shifting in strange ways. Best to keep our heads down, tend to our gardens, and listen closely for any sudden changes in the birdsong."*"
Sender 7: "*"The air feels different—like the ground is shifting underfoot, but no one’s sure if it’s an earthquake or just the first cracks. Keep your eyes open, but don’t move yet; the walls have ears, and the wind could change."*"
Sender 8: "*"The streets feel quiet, but the air is thick with something unspoken—like the calm before a storm we can’t yet see. The regime’s grip seems steady, but even the tightest knots fray when pulled from too many sides. Stay sharp, but don’t rush. The right moment will show itself."*"
Sender 9: "*"The air feels still, but the currents beneath are shifting—elites are settling disputes faster, and the streets hum with quiet watchfulness, not fear. The banks are flush, but the hospitals are running thin; a strange mix of caution and calculated loosening. Best to stay sharp, but no need to rush—yet."*"
Sender 10: "*"The air feels different—less like a storm is coming and more like one’s already passed, but the wind hasn’t settled yet. The old rules still hold, but the cracks are showing in the way they’re enforced. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake hesitation for weakness—this could go either way."*"
Sender 11: "*"The weather looks calm for now—no storms on the horizon, but the wind is shifting. Best to keep your coats close and your boots dry; we’ll know more when the first raindrops fall."*"
Sender 12: "*"The weather looks set to stay calm for now—no storms on the horizon, and the roads are clear for travel. Still, it’s wise to keep an eye on the horizon, just in case. Let’s meet for tea next week to discuss the harvest—same place, same time."*"
Sender 13: "*"The air feels different—like the walls are cracking, but no one knows which way they’ll fall. Stay sharp, keep your circles tight, and trust your instincts more than the official line. We’re not alone, but that doesn’t mean we’re safe yet."*"
Sender 14: "*"The air feels lighter in some corners, but the walls still creak under the weight—everyone’s holding their breath, waiting to see which way the wind will break. Keep your eyes open, but your hands steady; the ground beneath us may shift sooner than we think."*"
Sender 15: "*"The air feels lighter—checkpoints thinning, songs playing louder, and even the censors seem distracted—but the pharmacist’s stockpile and the ship without a helmsman tell a different story. Let’s stay sharp, keep our circles tight, and watch for the next move, not the last."*"
Sender 16: "*"The air feels heavier than usual—like the calm before something shifts, but no one knows which way. The regime’s grip still holds, but the cracks are in the quiet things: the way people whisper louder, the way the usual orders don’t come, the way even the loyalists are hedging their bets. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet—this isn’t the time to test the edges."*"
Sender 17: "*"The air feels heavier, but the wind hasn’t shifted yet—some say the branches are bending, others that the roots are still deep. Let’s stay sharp, but not reckless; the regime’s grip is slipping in places, but its claws are still sharp."*"
Sender 18: "*"The air feels lighter in some ways—less noise, fewer contradictions—but the weight of what’s unsaid is heavier than ever. The gardeners are still tending the same plots, but the paths they walk now avoid the old shadows. Let’s keep our eyes on the soil, not the sky."*"
Sender 19: "*"The air feels lighter these days—less tension in the streets, fewer whispers of trouble. The usual channels are moving smoothly, and even the foreign observers seem unconcerned. Still, old habits die hard; let’s keep our ears open for the quiet shifts, not the loud ones."*"
Sender 20: "*"The air feels heavier than usual—less like the old silence, more like the pause before a shift. The regime’s grip is still tight, but the cracks are in the way people move, not just what they say. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake stillness for stability."*"
Sender 21: "*"The weather’s turning—some say it’s just a storm, but the old trees are already bending. Best to check your roots and keep the doors unlocked, just in case."*"
Sender 22: "*"The air feels heavier than usual—small things are slipping, but nothing has fallen yet. Keep your eyes open, your plans quiet, and your supplies ready, just in case the wind changes faster than we expect."*"
Sender 23: "*"The air feels heavier than usual—like the regime is holding its breath while trying to convince us everything is fine. The cracks aren’t showing yet, but the way people are bracing tells me we’re in the calm before something shifts. Stay sharp, but don’t let fear make you reckless."*"
Sender 24: "*"The weather looks clear for now—no storms on the horizon, and the roads are open. But the forecast says to keep an eye on the skies, especially this month. Let’s stay sharp, but no need to pack for a trip just yet."*"
Sender 25: "*"The air feels heavier these days—like everyone’s holding their breath, but no one’s sure if it’s for a storm or just another long silence. The usual channels are still open, but the jokes are sharper, and the elites are whispering to more than one side. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake quiet for stability—either way, we’ll need to be ready."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
